description: This traditional Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is a comforting and nutritious staple in Middle Eastern homes, especially during colder months or Ramadan. Made with simple, wholesome ingredients like red lentils, vegetables, and a bright lemon finish, it offers a deeply satisfying flavor profile. It's a hearty, healthy, and naturally vegan dish that truly embodies the warmth of Lebanese hospitality.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Vegetables
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear, then drain well. Finely chop the onion and dice the carrots. Mince the garlic cloves, preparing all your ingredients for cooking.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and carrots, and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes. This step builds the flavor base for the soup.

instructions.title: Add Garlic and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in the minced garlic, ground cumin, and ground turmeric. Cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn the garlic. The spices will bloom and release their aromas into the vegetables.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Add the rinsed red lentils, vegetable broth (or water), salt, and black pepper to the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down.

instructions.title: Blend to Desired Consistency
instructions.text: Carefully use an immersion blender to partially or fully blend the soup to your desired consistency. For a smoother soup, blend completely until creamy. For a heartier texture, blend only half the soup, leaving some lentils whole.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the freshly squeezed lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed, adding more salt, pepper, or lemon juice to your preference. Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped cilantro or parsley and a drizzle of the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil, if desired.

tips: For an extra layer of authentic flavor, consider making a 'Tasha' (garlic-cilantro sauté) by frying extra garlic and cilantro in olive oil and swirling it into the soup just before serving.

While red lentils are traditional, you can substitute with yellow lentils if red are unavailable, though the cooking time might vary slightly. Always rinse lentils thoroughly to remove any debris and improve digestibility.

This soup tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It also freezes well for up to 3 months. Serve with warm pita bread or a side salad.
article:
Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known affectionately as Adas, is a cornerstone of Middle Eastern comfort food. This simple yet profoundly satisfying dish embodies the warmth, hospitality, and rich culinary heritage of the Levant. With its vibrant color, creamy texture, and zesty lemon finish, Adas is more than just a soup; it's a hug in a bowl, a nourishing meal that has graced family tables for generations. Whether you're seeking a hearty plant-based meal, a soothing remedy on a chilly day, or an authentic taste of Lebanese cuisine, this Lebanese Red Lentil Soup recipe promises to deliver. Let's dive into the world of this beloved Middle Eastern classic, exploring its origins, essential ingredients, and the simple steps to create your own perfect bowl of Adas.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas)?

At its heart, Adas simply means "lentils" in Arabic, but in the culinary context, it refers to this iconic red lentil soup. What sets Lebanese Red Lentil Soup apart is its characteristic smooth, velvety texture and its bright, tangy flavor profile, often enhanced by a generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice at the end. Unlike some other lentil soups that might be chunkier or heavily spiced, Lebanese Adas typically focuses on the pure flavor of the lentils, uplifted by sautéed onions and garlic, and a touch of salt and pepper. It’s naturally vegan and gluten-free, making it an accessible and wholesome option for almost everyone. This humble soup is a testament to how a few simple, high-quality ingredients can come together to create something truly extraordinary and deeply comforting.

## Ingredients You'll Need

Creating an authentic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup doesn't require an extensive shopping list. The beauty lies in the simplicity and quality of each component.

*   **Red Lentils:** 1 cup, dried (split red lentils are best as they cook quickly and break down easily).
*   **Olive Oil:** 2-3 tablespoons, extra virgin (for sautéing and drizzling).
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped.
*   **Garlic:** 3-4 cloves, minced.
*   **Vegetable Broth or Water:** 6-7 cups (broth adds more flavor).
*   **Lemon Juice:** 1/4 cup, freshly squeezed (or more, to taste).
*   **Salt:** 1-1.5 teaspoons, or to taste.
*   **Black Pepper:** 1/2 teaspoon, or to taste.
*   **Optional Garnish:** Fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped; crispy fried onions or pita croutons; a swirl of extra virgin olive oil.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is a straightforward process, perfect for beginner cooks and seasoned chefs alike. Follow these steps for a perfect bowl of Adas:

1.  **Rinse the Lentils:** Place the dried red lentils in a fine-mesh sieve and rinse thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any dust or debris. Set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Combine and Simmer:** Add the rinsed lentils to the pot, stirring them with the onions and garlic for about a minute. Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer gently for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have mostly broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
4.  **Blend (Optional, but Recommended):** For a smooth, creamy Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, use an immersion blender to purée the soup directly in the pot until it reaches your desired consistency. Alternatively, carefully transfer batches of the soup to a regular blender and blend until smooth. If using a regular blender, be cautious with hot liquids and only fill the blender halfway, venting the lid.
5.  **Season and Adjust:** Return the soup to the pot (if you used a regular blender). Stir in the fresh lemon juice, salt, and black pepper. Taste and adjust the seasonings as needed. You might want more lemon for a tangier soup, or more salt for flavor. If the soup is too thick, add a splash of hot water or broth until it reaches your preferred consistency.
6.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Adas into bowls. Garnish generously with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, a sprinkle of fresh chopped cilantro or parsley, and perhaps some crispy fried onions or pita croutons for added texture.

## Pro Tips for the Best Adas

While the recipe is simple, a few expert touches can elevate your Lebanese Red Lentil Soup from good to absolutely unforgettable.

*   **Don't Skimp on Lemon:** Fresh lemon juice is perhaps the most critical ingredient for authentic Lebanese Adas. It provides that essential bright, tangy finish that balances the earthiness of the lentils. Add it at the very end to preserve its freshness.
*   **Quality Olive Oil:** Use a good quality extra virgin olive oil, not just for sautéing but also for drizzling generously over the finished soup. It adds richness and a distinct Mediterranean flavor.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Seasoning is key. Always taste your soup before serving and adjust salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Lentils can absorb a lot of salt, so don't be afraid to add more if needed.
*   **Achieve the Right Consistency:** Some prefer their Lebanese Red Lentil Soup thicker, others slightly looser. If you blend it, aim for a creamy, pourable consistency. If it's too thick, add more hot broth or water until it's just right.
*   **Garnish with Care:** While optional, garnishes significantly enhance the experience. Crispy fried onions (often sold as "noodle hair" or "crispy fried onions" in Middle Eastern markets) add a wonderful textural contrast and savory depth. Fresh herbs like cilantro or parsley brighten the flavor.

## Serving Suggestions

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways:

*   **As a Main Course:** Served with warm pita bread for dipping, Adas makes a light yet filling meal on its own.
*   **As a Starter:** It's a perfect appetizer for a larger Middle Eastern feast, stimulating the palate without being too heavy.
*   **With a Side Salad:** Pair it with a simple fresh salad, such as a Fattoush or a basic cucumber and tomato salad, for a balanced and refreshing meal.
*   **Hearty Toppings:** Beyond traditional garnishes, consider adding a spoonful of plain yogurt (if not vegan), a sprinkle of sumac for extra tang, or even a dash of red pepper flakes for a subtle kick.

## Variations & Substitutions

While the classic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is cherished for its simplicity, there's always room for personal touches:

*   **Add Vegetables:** For extra nutrients and texture, you can add finely diced carrots, celery, or even a small potato along with the lentils. They will cook down and thicken the soup further.
*   **Spice It Up:** A pinch of ground cumin or coriander can add an earthy warmth, though traditionally, Lebanese Adas is kept simple. A tiny bit of turmeric can also enhance the golden color.
*   **Herbs:** While cilantro or parsley are common garnishes, some variations might include a touch of dried mint stirred in at the end for a refreshing aroma.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** A very small amount of smoked paprika can add a subtle depth, though this is not traditional.
*   **Gluten-Free & Vegan:** This soup is already naturally gluten-free and vegan, provided you use vegetable broth.

## Storage & Reheating Tips

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is an excellent make-ahead meal, as its flavors often deepen overnight.

*   **Refrigeration:** Store leftover Adas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
*   **Freezing:** This soup freezes beautifully. Allow it to cool completely, then transfer it to freezer-safe containers or bags. It can be frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.
*   **Reheating:** Reheat gently on the stovetop over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally. If the soup has thickened considerably, add a splash of water or vegetable broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Always add fresh lemon juice and garnishes when serving reheated soup to revive its vibrant flavors.

Embrace the comforting simplicity of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup. This nourishing and flavorful dish is a staple in Middle Eastern kitchens for good reason, offering a taste of tradition and wholesome goodness in every spoonful. Give this Adas recipe a try, and discover why this humble lentil soup holds such a special place in the hearts and homes of many. Sahtein! (To your health!)
